analysis.summary: New Zealand and Egypt meet in Vancouver in a pivotal Group G contest, with both sides sitting on one point after opening draws. Egypt drew 1-1 with Belgium on June 15, Emam Ashour scoring before a Hany own goal leveled. New Zealand produced a stunning 2-2 draw with Iran on June 16, with Eli Just becoming the first All White to score twice in a World Cup match. Despite being listed as 'home', New Zealand enjoy no genuine home advantage at BC Place; Egypt are heavy favorites on squad quality but NZ's resilience has been demonstrated.
analysis.home_form: New Zealand drew 2-2 with Iran (MD1, June 16): Eli Just scored in the 7th and 54th minutes, Iran equalized twice through Rezaeian (32nd) and Mohebbi (64th). Pre-tournament form was poor — nine defeats in 11 competitive matches between mid-2025 and early 2026 — but the World Cup showing against Iran showed tactical organization, a dangerous set-piece threat, and striking quality from Just and Chris Wood.
analysis.away_form: Egypt drew 1-1 with Belgium (MD1, June 15): Ashour struck in the 19th minute but a Hany own goal in the 66th off Lukaku's introduction gave Belgium a share. Egypt qualified impressively for the tournament, with Salah top-scoring in CAF qualifying (9 goals). Both Salah and Omar Marmoush are fit. Egypt reached the AFCON 2025 semi-finals, losing to Senegal. Squad quality — with Salah, Marmoush and Trezeguet — is clearly superior to New Zealand.
analysis.h2h: Egypt lead the all-time head-to-head 2W-1D-0L vs New Zealand across three senior meetings. Fixtures: a 1-1 friendly draw in 1999, a 1-0 Egypt win in a 1999 friendly, and a 1-0 Egypt win in the March 2024 FIFA Series. Total goals: 2 for Egypt, 1 for New Zealand across three matches — historically low-scoring encounters, with Egypt clinically efficient.
injuries_news: New Zealand: No confirmed injuries or suspensions. Chris Wood fit after a difficult club season with Nottingham Forest. Eli Just available after his brace vs Iran. Full squad available.

Egypt: Mohamed Salah fit (recovered from hamstring injury sustained in April 2026 at Liverpool). Omar Marmoush fit and available. No confirmed suspensions going into MD2. Full strength squad available.
key_factors: Group G context: All four teams level on 1 point after MD1. A win for either side is critical for top-two qualification; a draw leaves both needing results in MD3 vs Belgium and Iran respectively.
Egypt's attacking quality — Salah and Marmoush are Premier League and Champions League calibre, and face a New Zealand defense that conceded twice to Iran. Egypt will create chances.
New Zealand's defensive organization and set-piece threat: the 4-2-3-1 with Bell and Stamenic as a double pivot screens well; Chris Wood is dangerous aerially at corners and free kicks.
Altitude and climate: BC Place is a covered stadium at near sea level with artificial turf — no unusual environmental factor, though the turf may slightly favor Egypt's possession-based style.

Egypt must win to set up a favorable MD3 against Iran; a draw means they face Belgium needing a result, which is harder. This incentivizes Egypt to push forward, potentially opening space for NZ on the counter.
New Zealand's pre-tournament form was poor (9 losses in 11), but their MD1 performance vs Iran was significantly above expectations and may have raised confidence and morale.
